## 28. How To Talk While Solving

Coding interview mein **code sirf aadha marks** hai. Baaki aadha yeh hai ki interviewer aapki soch dekh paa raha hai ya nahi. Chup-chaap sahi solution likhne wala candidate aksar bolte hue thoda kam optimal solution likhne wale se **haar** jaata hai — kyunki hire karne ka faisla "yeh banda meri team mein debug kar payega?" par hota hai, "yeh banda LeetCode kar chuka hai?" par nahi.

### Interview ka minute-by-minute structure

| Time | Kya karna hai | Kya bolna hai |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 min | **Restate + clarify** | "So I'm given X and I need to return Y. Can I confirm — are the inputs sorted? Can there be duplicates? What should I return for an empty input?" |
| 3-5 min | **Example banao** | Ek chhota example khud likho aur expected output bolo. Agar aap khud example banate ho, aap ownership dikha rahe ho. |
| 5-8 min | **Brute force** | "The straightforward approach is... that's O(n squared) time. Let me see if I can do better before I write it." |
| 8-12 min | **Optimise, phir confirm** | Pattern ka naam bolo. "This is a sliding window — I'll expand right and shrink left when the condition breaks. Does that direction sound right to you?" |
| 12-30 min | **Code likho, bolte hue** | Har block ke pehle ek line: "Now I'll initialise the two pointers", "This handles the shrink case." |
| 30-35 min | **Dry run** | Apne hi example par line by line chalao. **Bug yahin milte hain, aur khud bug pakadna bahut strong signal hai.** |
| 35-40 min | **Complexity + edge cases** | Derive karke bolo. Phir empty, single element, all-same, negatives. |

### Exact phrases jo kaam karte hain

**Jab aap soch rahe ho (silence bharne ke liye):**

- "Let me think about the shape of this for a second — I want to say what I'm considering rather than go quiet."
- "My first instinct is a hash map, but let me check whether the array being sorted lets me avoid the extra space."
- "I'm weighing two approaches: one is O(n log n) with sorting, the other is O(n) with more space. Do you have a preference?"

**Jab aap phas gaye ho (yeh sabse important skill hai):**

- "I'm stuck on how to handle duplicates. Let me try a smaller example and see what breaks." — **phir actually chhota example likho.**
- "Let me go back to brute force and see which specific step is the expensive one." — yeh hamesha kaam karta hai.
- "Could I get a hint on whether I'm on the right track with the two-pointer idea?" — **hint maangna weakness nahi hai**, agar aap pehle 5 minute genuinely try kar chuke ho.

**Jab aapko bug mile:**

- "My dry run shows the wrong answer at index two — let me trace why." **Panic mat karo, khushi dikhao.** Bug milna acha hai.
- "I think the off-by-one is in the loop bound. Let me check what happens when the window is exactly size k."

**Jab aap khatam kar lo:**

- "That's O(n) time and O(k) space, where k is the number of distinct characters."
- "Edge cases I've handled: empty input returns zero, single element returns itself. One I haven't handled is integer overflow, which doesn't apply in Python but would in Java."
- "If the input were streaming instead of an array, I'd need to change this — happy to talk through that."

### Kya nahi karna hai

| Galti | Kyun kharaab hai | Iske badle |
|---|---|---|
| Chup-chaap 10 minute code likhna | Interviewer ko pata hi nahi chalta aap kahan ho, help nahi kar sakta | Har 30 second mein ek line bolo |
| Seedha optimal solution likh dena | Lagta hai yaad kiya hua hai; follow-up mein pakde jaaoge | Brute force pehle mention karo, 20 second mein |
| "This is easy" bolna | Agar phas gaye toh bahut bura lagta hai | "I've seen this shape before, let me work through it" |
| Interviewer ke hint ko ignore karna | Hint ka matlab hai aap galat raaste par ho | "That's a good point — let me follow that" |
| Complexity guess karna | Galat guess se poora solution shaqi ho jaata hai | Loops gino aur derive karo, out loud |
| Edge cases skip karna | **QA candidate ke liye yeh sabse bura signal hai** | Bina poochhe hi empty/null/duplicate bolo |
| Variable names `a`, `b`, `x` rakhna | Readability bhi assess hoti hai | `left`, `window_sum`, `char_count` |

### QA background ka faayda uthaao

Aap ek advantage ke saath aate ho jo pure-dev candidates ke paas nahi hai: **aap naturally sochte ho ki cheezein kaise toot sakti hain.** Isko chhupao mat, **highlight karo:**

- Code likhne se pehle edge cases list karo — yeh QA discipline hai aur interviewer ko turant dikhta hai.
- "If I were writing tests for this, the interesting cases would be..." — **yeh line QA candidates ke liye bahut strong hai.**
- Apne code ko dry run karke khud bug dhoondho, interviewer ke batane ka intezaar mat karo.
- Trade-offs system terms mein bolo: "this uses more memory but avoids a re-sort on every insert, which matters if writes are frequent."

### Aakhri baat

Aapko har problem solve karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. **Aapko yeh dikhana hai ki aap ek unfamiliar problem ke saath kaise pesh aate ho** — clarify karte ho, chhote example se sochte ho, brute force se shuru karke optimise karte ho, apna kaam khud verify karte ho, aur phasne par bina ghabraye structured tareeke se aage badhte ho. Yeh saari cheezein seekhi ja sakti hain, aur inhi par hire hota hai.

**All the best.**
